name: Framegen v1.5.5
body:
Stops the random freezes caused by the player's layout nudging the video by a few pixels.

- Small changes to the video's on-screen size (hover controls, a scrollbar, page reflow) no longer rebuild the frame pool and wipe the presentation queue. The pool now holds its size until a real resize such as fullscreen or theater mode.
- Model weights are unchanged.

name: Framegen v1.5.4
body:
Stops moving line art from ghosting on pans, and recovers smoothly after a scene cut.

- Panning scenes no longer double or ghost thin outlines. The static-text guard now steps aside wherever there is motion, so it only protects genuinely still parts of the frame.
- Hard scene cuts no longer stall for about half a second. The frame right after a cut keeps its presentation slot, and the pacing buffer absorbs delivery spikes instead of turning them into dropped frames.
- Adds a Flow upsample setting (Edge / Gated / Bilinear) under Enhancements; the default keeps current behavior.
- Model weights are unchanged.

name: Framegen v1.5.3
body:
Keeps static HUD and text from smearing, and stops Auto from falling back to the source rate.

- Static UI keeps a 4px halo. Motion removes that protection only where the color match is uncertain.
- Auto no longer treats upscale, or a measurement taken while paused, as proof the GPU cannot interpolate.
- Entering or leaving fullscreen no longer pins playback at the source frame rate.
- Twitch hover no longer flashes the side controls.
- Model weights are unchanged.

name: Framegen v1.5.1
body:
Keeps subtitles visible above generated frames.

- Adds Subtitle overlay under Player settings. It is on by default.
- Draws active text-track cues above the canvas, including in fullscreen.
- Raises detectable player caption layers while Framegen is running and restores them when it stops.
- Model weights are unchanged.

Thanks @NimaJafariComp for #21.

name: Framegen v1.5.0
body:
Lets Match display sit on the real panel rate, and keeps a short backlog instead of dropping it.

- Adds Full refresh rate in Advanced settings. Match display and Custom FPS use the measured refresh instead of 97% of it. Frames are still not scheduled faster than the screen.
- A 120Hz panel that the browser measures at about 118Hz can interpolate 60fps video again.
- Twitch theater mode and fullscreen keep the player controls above the canvas.
- A due backlog inside three output intervals is shown in order. Only older frames are dropped.
- Model weights are unchanged.

name: Framegen v1.4.7
body:
Fixes rare edge corruption in high-motion scenes and refreshes the in-player controls.

- Keeps the control island and settings panel inside the video across resizing, zoom, and fullscreen.
- Opens Advanced settings for very small players instead of squeezing the inline panel.
- Adds heavier collision, thin-edge, and anime-style regression coverage.
- Model weights and public runtime APIs are unchanged.

name: Framegen v1.4.6
body:
Improves source sharpness and makes Framegen and SR work consistently together.

- Preserves source-resolution detail through interpolation and presentation.
- Improves GPU workload accounting and safe texture reuse.
- Adds a reproducible VFI shootout harness.
- Model weights are unchanged.

Thanks @NimaJafariComp for #8.

name: v1.4.5
body: Improves Auto frame pacing on uneven and duplicate-heavy video.

name: v1.4.2 - FPS limit and settings polish
body:
Small extension-only update.

- Auto mode now has an optional FPS limit.
- Quick controls and Advanced settings are easier to use; profiles keep these choices.
- Added a toggle for non-critical in-player notices.

Models and weights are unchanged.

name: v1.4.1 - custom target FPS, profiles, and player compatibility
body:
## Custom target FPS, profiles, and player compatibility

Framegen 1.4.1 adds custom target rates, user-created profiles, and better compatibility with video players whose content does not fill the video element.

- Choose any Target FPS from 2 to 1000. The effective rate stays at least 2× the measured source cadence and is capped by real display, GPU, and runtime capacity. Auto, Display Hz, and fixed 2×–6× modes remain available.
- New full-page settings editor with local user-created profiles: create, duplicate, rename, apply, reset, and delete without silently changing the live setup.
- The FPS HUD and the small Framegen watermark can be hidden independently.
- The subtitle/static-text guard follows the real interpolation timestep while preserving guard-off parity and ordinary motion.
- Better player compatibility: `fill`, `contain`, `cover`, `none`, `scale-down`, and `object-position` are respected; source, resolution, and fullscreen transitions fail safely.
- Fresh clones can be loaded unpacked directly; release builds validate bundled runtimes and model payloads before packaging.
- v7s remains the default model. v6 remains as the legacy selectable option. Model weights are unchanged.

Thanks @NimaJafariComp for the player-compatibility and unpacked-install work in #1.

name: v1.4.0 - the calibration finally applies
body:
## The calibration finally applies - plus a runtime-wide perf pack

A performance release with byte-for-byte identical output (max|d|=0 in the A/B harness at every resolution, calm and motion; the model is untouched).

**The big one:** the one-shot kernel calibration persisted its result WITHOUT the w4/v2 flags - so every calibrated install has been running the legacy (pre-1.3.0) kernels for the interpolator and the untuned path for the upscaler. 1.4.0 re-calibrates once and the fast kernels actually stick.

Measured on an RTX 4060 Ti (same-run A/B vs 1.3.4, tune applied):

| | 1.3.4 | 1.4.0 |
|---|---|---|
| 2x cycle, 1080p | 4.98 ms | **3.75 ms (-25%)** |
| 2x cycle, 720p | 2.32 ms | **2.01 ms (-14%)** |
| SR 720p -> 1440p | 4.45 ms | **3.09 ms (-31%)** |
| SR 1080p -> 4K | 9.69 ms | **6.59 ms (-32%)** |
| calibration burst | ~3 s | **1.2-1.7 s** |

What changed:

- the tuner now sweeps the stride-2 conv0b shape too (w4 + 16-wide channel blocks take that kernel 0.92 -> 0.39 ms isolated at 1080p) and learns coc16 variants for the conv stack; tie-picks resolve to the incumbent shape
- the SR convs self-tune per video size - they ran the trunk's tune, a shape ~100x off theirs; the SR input conv reads exact texels instead of sampling
- calibration measures on GPU timestamps in watchdog-budgeted chunks: 2.4x shorter burst, same picks, wall-clock fallback kept
- web player: mids submit just-in-time for their display slot (the first mid no longer waits for the whole batch), the dedup readback no longer blocks the frame loop, tunes key per model, idle ladder rungs release their VRAM
- extension: SR skips marginal upscales (2x-then-downscale-to-the-same-size cost 3-9 ms per frame and was invisible), runtime rebuilds free the old VRAM immediately
- native/tools: the CUDA warp kernel no longer recompiles per call, trainers move uint8 batches and stopped syncing per step, dataset/eval IO overlaps the GPU

Tried and KILLED with numbers so nobody retries them blind: Winograd at this model's shapes, vec4 weight rows, f32 tile staging, a two-phase tuner prune - [docs/perf-2026-07-16.md](https://github.com/MONZikWasTaken/Framegen/blob/main/docs/perf-2026-07-16.md) has the full session log.

npm runtime: [`framegen@1.4.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) - `ConvTune` carries `w4`/`v2`/`s2` now, `RT` gains `destroy()`, `tuneConvRB` accepts `s2ci`. Weights are unchanged from 1.3.4 (the full sets ship as assets here, as on every minor).

name: v1.3.4 - compression-aware upscaler weights
body: New SR weights, same 27KB and same speed: the upscaler now cleans compression artifacts instead of sharpening them (the old weights scored BELOW bilinear on compressed input). Trained on film + anime (ATD-12K) with a JPEG degradation ladder. Real-pipeline numbers: clean 34.57 -> 35.17 dB, degraded-input 29.28 -> 29.54 dB. npm: framegen@1.3.4 (weights ship in the package).

name: v1.3.3 - fullscreen buttons, consistent upscale, FG branding
body: Patch: side buttons no longer get squashed by fullscreen player CSS; the upscaler now processes every presented frame (was generated-frames-only - visible sharpness shimmer on low-res video); the button says FG now. Known: on heavily compressed 360p sources the current 27KB SR model amplifies compression artifacts around edges - that is the model's ceiling, new weights are the fix and are in the training plan.

name: v1.3.2 - scale-general upscaler + quality baseline
body: SR patch: the upscale factor is decided by the weights (1x restore / 2x / 4x pixel-shuffle), quality harness added (current 2x model: +1.05dB over bicubic, verified), envelope benches for the future student. npm: framegen@1.3.2 (createSR exposes .scale).

name: v1.3.1 - upscaler on the fast kernels
body:
Patch: the 2x upscaler (SR) now runs on the same optimized kernels as the interpolator - it was still on the legacy conv path while running at FULL video resolution.

Measured on an RTX 4060 Ti, per presented frame, bit-identical output:

| | 1.3.0 | 1.3.1 |
|---|---|---|
| 720p -> 1440p | 7.7 ms | **4.1 ms** |
| 1080p -> 4K | 18.1 ms | **9.1 ms** |

SR at 1440p now fits comfortably alongside 2x interpolation in a 60 fps budget.

npm runtime: [`framegen@1.3.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) (createSR accepts the tuner's `convTune`).

name: v1.3.0 - the convert bottleneck falls
body:
## The convert bottleneck falls

A deep kernel audit found the real limiter of the conv stack: not memory, but **f16-to-f32 conversions** - quarter-rate on modern NVIDIA. This release removes them from the hot loop entirely, plus a texture-path rework. Same pixels: the new conv kernel is **bit-exact**; the texture pass differs by at most 1 LSB on 0.1% of bytes (the same accepted class as 1.1.0's direct-warp).

Measured on an RTX 4060 Ti at 720p, tuned, same-run A/B vs 1.2.0:

| | 1.2.0 | 1.3.0 |
|---|---|---|
| per generated frame | 0.94 ms | **0.78 ms (-17%)** |
| trunk per source pair | 1.89 ms | **1.44 ms (-24%)** |
| full 2x cycle | 2.67 ms | **2.19 ms (-18%)** |

Since yesterday's 1.1.1 that compounds to **-32% per generated frame**.

What changed:
- **New autotuner kernel variants**: the thread's 4x4 input window lives in registers (16 tile ops per channel instead of 36) and weights arrive pre-widened to f32 - an isolated conv dispatch dropped from 1.25 ms to 0.20 ms (6.2x). The tuner still measures and picks per GPU; nothing is hardcoded.
- **Flow/mask/residual planes are filterable textures now**: the upsampling in the composite and refine passes runs through the hardware bilinear unit (one sample instead of 20 buffer reads), and the per-frame 691 KB buffer clear became a render-pass fast clear.
- Stored kernel calibrations from older versions recalibrate automatically (the kernel generation changed).
- Fixed: black flashes while the SR upscaler compiled its per-size pipelines; SR breaking permanently after many resolution switches; two bind-group cache bugs that could crash presentation after 48+ texture rebuilds; VRAM leaks in the player's SR rings.

npm runtime: [`framegen@1.3.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) - same API, no breaking changes.

name: v1.2.0 - same pixels, less GPU
body:
## Same pixels, less GPU

A pure performance release: the runtime got a kernel-level pass and produces **byte-for-byte identical output** to 1.1.1 (v7s; v6 differs by max 1 LSB on 0.00% of bytes). Measured on an RTX 4060 Ti at 720p, tuned config, wall-clock:

| | 1.1.1 | 1.2.0 |
|---|---|---|
| per generated frame | 1.14 ms | **0.94 ms (-18%)** |
| full 2x cycle | 3.13 ms | **2.67 ms (-15%)** |

At high factors (display-Hz mode, up to 19 generated frames per source pair) the per-frame saving multiplies.

What changed under the hood:
- **Deconv rewritten** (0.20 -> 0.07 ms): one thread computes all 5 output channels instead of a 5x z-fan-out re-reading the same window; the whole weight tensor stages through workgroup memory; stride-2 tap parity resolved up front.
- **conv0b on a register-blocked stride-2 kernel** - 3.8x in isolation (the old path re-read every input texel ~9x per z-slice from global memory).
- **FiLM fused into cb6's tile load** - one less dispatch per generated frame, bit-exact arithmetic.
- **Zero-copy chain**: both per-pair 691 KB buffer snapshots are gone (the residual and the trunk stash are written in place).
- Refine convs pack 8 channels per thread; autotuner compiles variants async (no more calibration jank) and gained a new kernel variant (measured per GPU, never assumed).
- VRAM: f32 originals of f16-converted weights are freed (~3 MB), fixed a present-blit crash after 48+ texture rebuilds, removed forced-layout hot spots in the content script.
- New `web/bench.html` - the A/B harness behind every number above (byte-parity check, per-stage GPU timestamps).

npm runtime: [`framegen@1.2.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) - same API, no breaking changes; existing integrations get the speedup by bumping the version.

name: v1.1.1 - MIT relicense
body:
## MIT relicense

Framegen's code is now **MIT** - the extension and the [`framegen`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) npm runtime. Embed it in anything, commercial included, no copyleft (was AGPLv3 for the app / LGPL for the library).

- Extension bumped to **1.1.1** to match the runtime - **no functional change** from 1.1.0 (same direct-warp + occlusion-sparse refine, same parity).
- The extension bundle now ships a `LICENSE` (MIT) inside the zip.
- npm runtime republished as [`framegen@1.1.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) (MIT metadata; code identical to 1.1.0).

**Model weights stay non-commercial** ([WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md](https://github.com/MONZikWasTaken/Framegen/blob/main/WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md)) - they are distilled from a RIFE-family teacher whose license chain isn't clean enough to free them yet. A fully-free weight set is on the roadmap.

If you want the runtime behavior details, see [v1.1.0](https://github.com/MONZikWasTaken/Framegen/releases/tag/v1.1.0).

name: v1.1.0 - direct-warp + occlusion-sparse refine
body:
## Faster on every GPU, much faster on calm content

- **Direct-warp flowout**: warps now sample the source frames straight through the texture units instead of a full-res f32 copy - the `imgs` buffer (up to 50 MB VRAM at 1080p) and its prep pass are gone, and mids are resampled once instead of twice (slightly sharper).
- **Occlusion-sparse refine**: the refine head only repairs pixels where the two warps disagree - so now it only RUNS there. A GPU-side scheduler thresholds per-tile disagreement and feeds the conv chain through `dispatchWorkgroupsIndirect`; no CPU roundtrip. Bit-identical output on full-motion frames; on calm shots (anime, talking heads, streams) the refine chain drops ~4x and a mid costs up to **-34%** (measured at 720p, RTX 4060 Ti).
- Static-region guard is now computed once per frame pair instead of per generated frame (up to 19x less work in display-Hz mode).
- Kernel autotuner explores more workgroup shapes and runs at idle instead of 4 s into playback (no more drop burst right after enabling).
- Fixed: switching the model (v6/v7 small) in the panel now actually hot-swaps the runtime.
- Added 90/360 Hz to display-match mode; smoother stats and fewer forced layouts on heavy pages.
- npm runtime updated: [`framegen@1.1.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) (new `sparseRefine`/`refineThr` options, `rt.profileT()` per-stage GPU profiler).

Parity vs 1.0.0: mean|d| <= 0.08, max|d| <= 7 on the reference pair (resampling semantics change - single resample instead of double); bit-exact at matching resolutions.


---

**License:** the Framegen code is now **MIT** (was AGPLv3; the runtime library was LGPL) - embed it anywhere, commercial included. Model weights stay under their separate non-commercial terms ([WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md](https://github.com/MONZikWasTaken/Framegen/blob/main/WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md)). npm runtime republished as [`framegen@1.1.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/framegen) (MIT metadata; runtime code identical to 1.1.0).

name: Framegen v1.0.0
body:
Real-time neural frame interpolation in the browser. A Chrome extension that
takes any `<video>` on any page and plays it at 2x-6x the frame rate - a
distilled 2.9 MB model on a hand-written WGSL/WebGPU runtime, entirely on
your GPU. No servers, no accounts, nothing leaves your computer.

## Highlights

- **2x-6x more frames** on YouTube and most video sites; ~3 ms per generated
  frame on a mid-range GPU (RTX 4060 Ti)
- **Auto mode**: an adaptive controller picks the highest factor your GPU and
  display actually sustain - it backs off before you would see a stutter
- **Anime mode**: detects animation drawn "on twos" and interpolates the real
  motion; scene-cut detection never blends across cuts
- **Display-Hz mode**: output locked to your monitor's refresh grid (built
  for 120-240 Hz screens)
- **Compare slider**: original on the left, Framegen on the right
- **Optional neural 2x upscale** (TinySR) of the generated frames
- Works in vertical feeds (Shorts/TikTok) and survives mid-roll ads and
  quality switches
- Two model generations in the selector: v7 small (default) and v6

## Install

**Easiest: [add to Chrome from the Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/framegen-frame-interpolat/hpdpcjakhclhljfdkpjolonjlopbdhfk)** - one click, auto-updates.

Manual (this zip):

1. Download `framegen-extension.zip` below and extract it.
2. `chrome://extensions` -> enable **Developer mode** -> **Load unpacked** ->
   select the extracted folder.

Requires Chrome 121+ and a GPU. Details, numbers and the full technical story:
[README](https://github.com/MONZikWasTaken/Framegen#readme) /
[docs/TECHNICAL.md](https://github.com/MONZikWasTaken/Framegen/blob/main/docs/TECHNICAL.md).

`bbb_60fps_v7s.mp4` attached below is genuine model output (the README hero
clip): the 15 fps eval clip interpolated 4x to 60 fps by the shipped weights.
